*** Add File: /home/wlia0047/ar57/wenyu/GeneRec/results/research/issue121/rounds/round_20261028_065943_250/agents/scoring_2/scores.txt
+SCORE: interest_signature_hypball | behavior_evidence=4 | geometry_necessity=3 | novelty=3 | downstream_mechanism=4 | falsifiability=2 | implementability=3 | exploration_value=3
+SCOPE: interest_signature_hypball | OUT_OF_SCOPE | Behavior and Poincare scoring are computationally coupled, but the proposal does not specify behavior-off, geometry-off/Euclidean, and both-on switches/comparisons as part of the mechanism; it only specifies the both-on computation. Add these exact switch paths, keeping all other computation matched.
+EVIDENCE: interest_signature_hypball | E1 E2 E3 E5 E6 E8 E9 E10 E12 E13 E14
+OBJECTION: interest_signature_hypball | The hashed cohort-to-parent restriction can dominate the learned content geometry: a poor or arbitrary hash assigns items to disjoint first-level code subsets, and the stated fixed-curvature Poincare operation then cannot compare across those subsets. The evidence supports cohort-profile signal, but does not establish that hashing users into M cohorts captures the measured signal.
+COUNTEREXAMPLE: interest_signature_hypball | With M=2, suppose the same transition-role users are split evenly by hash, while two items have identical latent z and identical true use; add-one smoothing can make their maximum-mass cohort differ by one count. Their candidate code sets are then disjoint despite identical content and role, so the restriction—not curved distance—forces different first tokens.
+RATIONALE: interest_signature_hypball | behavior_evidence=4 because measured cohort-profile overlap separates positives from negatives (E9), but the proposal's hashed-user cohorts are not the measured 64 successor-cohort profile, so support is not fully transferable. geometry_necessity=3: log/exp maps and geodesic scoring act in the coupled first-token path (E12-E14), but a matched Euclidean displacement and cancellation analysis are absent. novelty=3: a continuous behavior-shifted point plus restricted curved assignment is computationally distinct in this bundle; external prior-art/ledger comparison is UNKNOWN, resolved by a bounded comparison against the cited work and local mechanism ledger. downstream_mechanism=4: cohort-derived shift and candidate restriction change first-token assignments while later residual levels retain identity; expected prefix predictability/assignment change is diagnostic. falsifiability=2 because the three named switch conditions are not specified as matched executable controls. implementability=3: computational outline and fixed projection are stated, but projection/map clipping at the ball boundary and safe codeword constraints are not specified; check implementation safeguards and actual batch/codebook dimensions before the single run. exploration_value=3: distinct user-cohort path, with informative hash-noise failure mode. No prediction of Recall is made.
+
+SCORE: flow_barycenter_geodesic_bottleneck | behavior_evidence=3 | geometry_necessity=3 | novelty=3 | downstream_mechanism=4 | falsifiability=2 | implementability=3 | exploration_value=3
+SCOPE: flow_barycenter_geodesic_bottleneck | OUT_OF_SCOPE | The successor-flow barycentre is translated through Mobius addition and geodesic assignment, so the core coupling is present; however, behavior-off, geometry-off/Euclidean, and both-on switches/comparisons are not specified as part of the mechanism. Add those paths and matched comparison definitions.
+EVIDENCE: flow_barycenter_geodesic_bottleneck | E1 E2 E3 E5 E6 E7 E12 E13
+OBJECTION: flow_barycenter_geodesic_bottleneck | The proposal relies on a successor-embedding barycentre being a meaningful displacement in the latent tangent space, but the evidence measures successor entropy and prior mechanisms, not alignment between frozen input-embedding barycentres and the encoder-latent directions.
+COUNTEREXAMPLE: flow_barycenter_geodesic_bottleneck | If two successor items have frozen embeddings x and -x with equal transition weight, their normalized weighted mean is zero (or undefined if normalization is attempted before centering); the behavior translation vanishes despite a nontrivial successor distribution, leaving the first-level computation effectively content-only for that item.
+RATIONALE: flow_barycenter_geodesic_bottleneck | behavior_evidence=3: training successor structure is measured, including strong entropy stratification (E5), but there is no measured evidence that embedding barycentres align with useful next-token roles. geometry_necessity=3: Mobius translation, exp map, and geodesic assignment are explicit (E12-E13), but a matched Euclidean control argument and cancellation analysis are missing. novelty=3: continuous per-item successor barycentre translation before an unrestricted global quantizer differs computationally from a discrete partition; external prior-art/ledger trace is UNKNOWN, bounded check: compare the exact computation with cited work and local ledger. downstream_mechanism=4: translation changes first-token assignment while unshifted residual input is intended to preserve identity; assignments and prefix predictability are named diagnostics. falsifiability=2 because the required switch controls are not specified. implementability=3: broadly implementable, but zero/cancelled barycentres, ball projection/clipping and the precise scale/curvature numerical guards require bounded implementation checks. exploration_value=3: tests continuous barycentric translation rather than a discrete behavior partition; failure would inform whether this displacement is useful. No Recall prediction is made.
+
+SCORE: transition-radial-sector-vq | behavior_evidence=3 | geometry_necessity=3 | novelty=2 | downstream_mechanism=4 | falsifiability=2 | implementability=3 | exploration_value=2
+SCOPE: transition-radial-sector-vq | OUT_OF_SCOPE | Popularity-adjusted successor profiles condition sector prototypes and Poincare assignment, so there is a coupled pathway; nevertheless the required behavior-off, geometry-off/Euclidean, and both-on switches/comparisons are not specified. Add these controls as actual code paths, with matched remaining computations.
+EVIDENCE: transition-radial-sector-vq | E1 E2 E3 E5 E6 E7 E12 E13 E14
+OBJECTION: transition-radial-sector-vq | The behavior-sector constraint and prototype addition may largely determine assignments before hyperbolic geometry contributes, while the measured prior successor-geodesic coarse variants were below the reported l1-only/resample reference on beam-survival evidence (E6); this proposal does not establish why its sector/prototype variant avoids that failure mode.
+COUNTEREXAMPLE: transition-radial-sector-vq | For two items with identical latent z but different sector labels whose allocated code sets are disjoint, sector restriction forces different first tokens even if the Poincare distances to a code in the other sector would be smaller; thus geodesic scoring cannot undo the discrete behavior partition.
+RATIONALE: transition-radial-sector-vq | behavior_evidence=3: successor distributions and entropy stratification are measured (E5), but evidence does not measure this KL-sector assignment or its predictive value. geometry_necessity=3: fixed-curvature exp maps and geodesic distances are explicit in the assignment (E12-E14), but the proposal does not argue added value against a matched Euclidean counterpart or rule out sector restriction as the effective operation. novelty=2: behavior-defined sectors plus curved within-sector VQ are a routine variation of discrete behavior-conditioned candidate sets/coarse assignments in the supplied mechanism family; external prior-art status is UNKNOWN, resolvable by a bounded ledger/cited-work comparison. downstream_mechanism=4: sector prototypes and restricted first-level assignment are expected to change first tokens, while residual levels retain identity; the diagnostics are named. falsifiability=2 because the three required switches are not specified. implementability=3: steps are mostly specified, but sparse KL smoothing, empty/zero profiles, PCA sign/basis determinism and finite-ball projection safeguards need concrete implementation checks. exploration_value=2: close to existing successor-geodesic coarse and behavior-restricted mechanisms (E6), though with a sector-prototype variant. No Recall prediction is made.
*** End Patch
